In [[economics]], the '''consumption distribution''' or '''consumption inequality''' is an alternative to the [[income distribution]] or [[wealth distribution]] for judging [[economic inequality]], comparing levels of [[Consumption (economics)|consumption]] or spending rather than [[income]] or [[wealth]].<ref>{{cite web | title=OECD Framework for Statistics on the Distribution of Household Income, Consumption and Wealth | website=OECD iLibrary | date=2006-06-16 | url=https://www.oecd-ilibrary.org/economics/framework-for-statistics-on-the-distribution-of-household-income-consumption-and-wealth_9789264194830-en | access-date=2024-09-01}}</ref> This is an important measure of inequality as the basic utility of the wealth or income is the expenditure.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://web.stanford.edu/~pista/JEP.pdf|title=Consumption Inequality|author1=Orazio P. Attanasio|author2=Luigi Pistaferri}}</ref> People [[experience]] the inequality directly in consumption, rather than income or wealth.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jpmorganchase.com/institute/research/cities-local-communities/insight-consumption-inequality|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240124121200/www.jpmorganchase.com/institute/research/cities-local-communities/insight-consumption-inequality|archive-date=2024-01-24|title=RESEARCH - Consumption Inequality - What's in Your Shopping Basket?}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Daşdemir |first=Esat |date=2025-06-21 |title=Inflation and consumption inequality |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s43546-025-00850-7 |journal=SN Business & Economics |language=en |volume=5 |issue=7 |article-number=89 |doi=10.1007/s43546-025-00850-7 |issn=2662-9399|url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[World Bank]] lists 118 countries  based on consumption inequality compared to 68 countries based on [[income inequality]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Haddad |first=Cameron Nadim |last2=Mahler |first2=Daniel Gerszon |last3=Diaz-Bonilla |first3=Carolina |last4=Hill |first4=Ruth |last5=Lakner |first5=Christoph |last6=Ibarra |first6=Gabriel Lara |date=June 2024 |title=The World Bank’s New Inequality Indicator: The Number of Countries with High Inequality |url=https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099549506102441825/pdf/IDU-bd155bac-6d78-43af-8833-f87564a9d6c8.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250503224135/https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099549506102441825/pdf/IDU-bd155bac-6d78-43af-8833-f87564a9d6c8.pdf |archive-date=2025-05-03 |website=[[World Bank]]}}</ref>{{AI-retrieved source|date=January 2026}}
